standard_prerequisites.name: Dominant rational map between varieties
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, Definition labelled morphisms-definition-dominant-rational (canonical Stacks tag 0A1Z) together with the discussion following it; invoked at proof lines 173-176
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the characterisation of dominant rational maps as those rational maps sending the generic point of the source to the generic point of the target, which is what makes the functor on function fields well defined.

standard_prerequisites.name: A local map of function fields determines a unique dominant rational map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-rational-map-finite-presentation (canonical Stacks tag 0BX8); invoked at proof lines 184-186
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the converse direction, hence full faithfulness of the functor.

core_obligations: Build the functor: for varieties X and Y with generic points x and y, a dominant rational map X contained in U -> Y sends x to y, and hence induces a k-algebra map k(Y) = kappa(y) -> kappa(x) = k(X) of function fields (proof lines 172-183).

Full faithfulness: conversely every such k-algebra map (automatically local, since source and target are fields) determines a unique dominant rational map, so the assignment is fully faithful (proof lines 184-187).

Essential image: for a finitely generated field extension K/k choose a finite type k-algebra A contained in K with K its fraction field; then X = Spec(A) is a variety with function field K, which shows every object of the target category is hit (proof lines 188-192).
proof_roadmap: Identify dominant rational maps with those carrying the generic point to the generic point, and read off the induced map of function fields (proof lines 172-183).
Use the cited lemma to invert that assignment and conclude full faithfulness (proof lines 184-187).
Realise a finitely generated extension as the function field of Spec(A) for a suitable finite type algebra A (proof lines 188-192).
difficulty_reason: The theorem asserts an equivalence between two categories: varieties over k with dominant rational maps, and finitely generated field extensions K/k (statement lines 166-168). The proof has to do two different jobs, and the difficulty is in seeing that they suffice: full faithfulness comes from reading a dominant rational map as the induced map of function fields k(Y) -> k(X) at the generic points and inverting it with the cited lemma on rational maps of finite presentation, while the essential image needs the separate observation that a finitely generated extension is the fraction field of a finite type k-algebra A, so that Spec(A) is a variety having K as its function field (proof lines 172-192). Neither direction is a computation; both are structural, which is why the claim is H2 and not lower.
